Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-1512", "title": "Diphtheria", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Diphtheria is a serious bacterial infection."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "You can catch it from a person who has the infection and coughs or sneezes."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You can also get infected by coming in contact with an object, such as a toy, that has bacteria on it."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Diphtheria usually affects the nose and throat."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Symptoms include: Sore throat Swollen glands in the neck Fever Weakness Your doctor will diagnose it based on your signs and symptoms and a lab test."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Getting treatment for diphtheria quickly is important."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "If your doctor suspects that you have it, you'll start treatment before the lab tests come back."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus vaccine can prevent diphtheria, but its protection does not last forever."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Children need another dose, or booster, at about age 12."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Then, as adults, they should get a booster every 10 years."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Diphtheria is very rare in the United States because of the vaccine."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5331", "title": "Salivary Gland Cancer", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your salivary glands make saliva - sometimes called spit - and empty it into your mouth through openings called ducts."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Saliva makes your food moist, which helps you chew and swallow."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It also cleans your mouth and contains antibodies that can kill germs."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Salivary gland cancer is a type of head and neck cancer ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It may not cause any symptoms, or you could notice: A lump in your ear, cheek, jaw, lip, or inside the mouth Fluid draining from your ear Trouble swallowing or opening the mouth widely Numbness, weakness, or pain in your face Doctors diagnose salivary gland cancer using a physical exam, imaging tests, and a biopsy."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Treatment can include surgery, radiation therapy, and/or chemotherapy."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1618", "title": "Tendinitis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Tendons are flexible bands of tissue that connect muscles to bones."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Tendinitis is the severe swelling of a tendon."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Tendinitis usually happens after repeated injury to an area such as the wrist or ankle."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It causes pain and soreness around a joint."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some common forms of tendinitis are named after the sports that increase their risk."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "They include tennis elbow, golfer's elbow, pitcher's shoulder, swimmer's shoulder, and jumper's knee."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Doctors diagnose tendinitis with your medical history, a physical exam, and imaging tests."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The first step in treatment is to reduce pain and swelling."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Rest, wrapping or elevating the affected area, and medicines can help."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Ice is helpful for recent, severe injuries."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Other treatments include ultrasound, physical therapy, steroid injections, and surgery."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1686", "title": "Hepatitis A", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Inflammation is swelling that happens when tissues of the body are injured or infected."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "This swelling and damage can affect how well your liver functions."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Hepatitis A is a type of viral hepatitis."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It causes an acute, or short-term, infection."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "This means that people usually get better without treatment after a few weeks."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Thanks to a vaccine, hepatitis A is not very common in the United States."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Hepatitis A is caused by the hepatitis A virus."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The virus spreads through contact with an infected person's stool."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "This can happen if you: Eat food made by someone who has the virus and did not properly wash their hands after using the bathroom Drink contaminated water or eat foods that were rinsed with contaminated water Have close personal contact with someone who has hepatitis A."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "This could be through certain types of sex (like oral-anal sex), taking care of someone who is ill, or using illegal drugs with others."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Although anyone can get hepatitis A, you are at higher risk if you: Travel to developing countries Have sex with someone who has hepatitis A Are a man who has sex with men Use illegal drugs Are experiencing homelessness Live with or care for someone who has hepatitis A Live with or care for a child recently adopted from a country where hepatitis A is common What are the symptoms of hepatitis A?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Not everyone with hepatitis A has symptoms."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Adults are more likely to have symptoms than children."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "If you do have symptoms, they usually start 2 to 7 weeks after infection."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They can include: Dark yellow urine Diarrhea Fatigue Fever Gray- or clay-colored stools Joint pain Loss of appetite Nausea and/or vomiting Abdominal pain Yellowish eyes and skin, called jaundice The symptoms usually last less than 2 months, although some people can be ill for as long as 6 months."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "You are at a higher risk of getting a more severe infection from hepatitis A if you also have HIV , hepatitis B , or hepatitis C ."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What other problems can hepatitis A cause?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "In rare cases, hepatitis A may lead to liver failure."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "This is more common in adults over age 50 and in people who have another liver ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "To diagnose hepatitis A, your health care provider may use many tools: A medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms A physical exam Blood tests, including tests for viral hepatitis What are the treatments for hepatitis A?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "There is no specific treatment for hepatitis A."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "The best way to recover is to rest, drink plenty of liquids, and eat healthy foods."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Your provider may also suggest medicines to help relieve symptoms."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "In more severe cases, you may need care in a hospital."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "The best way to prevent hepatitis A is to get the hepatitis A vaccine."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "It is also important to have good hygiene , especially washing your hands thoroughly after you go to the bathroom."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-285", "title": "Heroin", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Heroin is an illegal, very addictive opioid drug ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It's made from morphine, which comes from the seedpod of opium poppy plants."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "These plants grow in Southeast and Southwest Asia, Mexico, and Colombia."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Heroin can be a white or brown powder, or a black sticky substance known as black tar heroin."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "People inject, sniff, snort, or smoke heroin."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Some people mix heroin with crack cocaine , which is called \"speedballing.\" All these ways of taking heroin send it to the brain very quickly, which makes it highly addictive."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "What are the short-term effects of heroin?"}, {"id": "S007", "text": "People who use heroin report feeling a \"rush\" (a surge of pleasure)."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "And then they may feel other effects, such as a warm flushing of the skin, dry mouth , and a heavy feeling in the arms and legs."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "They may also have severe itching , nausea, and vomiting ."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "After these first effects, they will usually be drowsy for several hours, and their breathing will slow down."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "What are the long-term effects of heroin?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "People who use heroin over the long term may develop many different health problems."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "These problems could include liver , kidney , and lung disease, mental disorders , and abscesses ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "People who inject the drug also risk getting infectious diseases such as HIV , hepatitis , and bacterial infections of the skin, bloodstream, and heart ( endocarditis )."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "When a vein collapses, the blood cannot flow through it."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Repeated use of heroin can lead to tolerance."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "This means users need more and more of the drug to have the same effect."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "At higher doses over time, the body becomes dependent on heroin."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "If someone who is dependent on heroin stops using it, they have withdrawal symptoms."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "These symptoms can include restlessness, muscle and bone pain, diarrhea , vomiting, and cold flashes with goose bumps."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Repeated use of heroin often leads to heroin use disorder, sometimes called addiction."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "It's a chronic (long-lasting) brain disorder."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "When someone has it, they continue to use heroin even though it causes problems in their life."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Some examples include health problems and not being able to meet responsibilities at work, school, or home."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Getting and using heroin becomes their main purpose in life."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "This happens when a person uses so much heroin that it causes a life-threatening reaction or death."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "All heroin users are at risk of an overdose because they never know the actual strength of the drug they are taking or what may have been added to it."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Most heroin available in the United States is combined with illegally made fentanyl (IMF)."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Using heroin combined with IMF, or along with other drugs or alcohol can increase the risk of an overdose."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "When people overdose on heroin, their heart rate and breathing slow down."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Their breathing may slow do so much that not enough oxygen reaches the brain."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Hypoxia can lead to a coma , permanent brain damage, or death."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "A medicine called naloxone can treat a heroin (or other opioid) overdose if it is given in time."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "It works by blocking the effects of the opioid on the body."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Sometimes more than one dose of the medicine is needed."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "There are two forms of naloxone that anyone can use without medical training: nasal spray and injectable."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "People at risk of an overdose are encouraged to carry naloxone with them."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "What are the treatments for heroin use disorder?"}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Treatments for heroin use disorder include medicines to treat withdrawal symptoms, medicine to block the effects of opioids, and behavioral treatments."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Often, a combination of medicine and behavioral treatment works best."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "People getting treatment for heroin use disorder should work with their health care providers to come up with a treatment plan that fits their needs."}]}]
